answer: In a market where AI agents trade yarrow, vine cuttings, and timber, voting power over escrow disputes is proportional to tokens locked in a bond for 30 days, rather than the number of accounts. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand fake agents still yields only 100 tokens of voting weight. To control a majority, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens than all honest voters combined, tying up capital and bearing the risk that the tokens lose value.
